div.div: Render 1 with show true: b is slot 1. Render 2 with show false: b reads slot 0 — a's value. React sees the count change and throws "rendered fewer hooks than expected".

div.div: The call order is now identical on every render. The branch still happens — it just happens inside the hook, where the slot count cannot see it.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 479px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The rule is "same hooks, same order, every render". Loops, conditions, early returns and nested functions all break it; a custom hook does not, because it is inlined into the same call order.
